title: Small house on posts, from Jim's pencil sketch

reasons.above_grade_mm: the sketch's '?' from grade to the floor; Jim's word gives it
reasons.section_mm: the post stock gives it: post_stock is the catalog's 6x6 UC4B post, dressed 5-1/2 in (wt.dressed_sizes); a number here overrides it

reasons.thickness_mm: the panel gives it: panel is the sold 4.625 in Acme SIP, 4 by 12 ft (Jim, 2026-10-25: the world takes the sold thickness, nothing invented); Jim's floor build-up may override it
reasons.elevation_mm: the construction domain lays the floor's top at the datum, so a null here lies the panel its thickness below it

reasons.height_mm: reading: the south elevation's '12' as wall height, floor top to roof underside; 12 ft overall above grade is the other reading
reasons.thickness_mm: the panel gives it: panel is the sold 4.625 in Acme SIP, 4 by 12 ft (Jim, 2026-10-25: the world takes the sold thickness, nothing invented); a number here overrides it
reasons.panel_width_mm: 4 ft is a sold width (sip.stock.premier_widths, sip.stock.acme_sizes); chosen narrow for handling and take-down; open for ranking

reasons.south_eave_mm: reading: the hatched hangover on the south, 8 ft past the floor; centred, 5 ft each end, is the other reading
reasons.east_eave_mm: the sketch's 12 ft roof width less the 8 ft floor and the 2 ft west eave
reasons.thickness_mm: the roof panel gives it: roof_panel is the sold 8.25 in Acme SIP, 4 by 12 ft (Jim, 2026-10-25: sold stock, nothing invented); a number here overrides it

reasons.sides: Jim, 2026-10-18: only south-facing glass; no east, west or north window
reasons.first_sill_mm: Jim: the first 4 ft of the south wall is a SIP panel below the windows
reasons.glazed_height_mm: Jim: 8 ft of glass over the knee wall
reasons.rows: Jim: two stacked 4x8 windows, the upper one lighting the sleeping loft; one row (one 8x8) or two rows of two columns (four 4x4) fill the same 8 ft
reasons.columns: Jim: each window spans the south wall's 8 ft

reasons.sun_watt_per_square_metre: assumed clear-sky peak; the solver applies it to every side

reasons.mean_reflectance: assumed mid-grey interior; Jim's wall finish gives it
reasons.sky_angle_degrees: assumed open sky; the site gives it

reasons.width_mm: Jim, 2026-10-18: the north door's framing is 4 ft wide by 8 ft tall
reasons.height_mm: Jim: 8 ft tall door framing; a 4 ft tall 8 ft wide SIP panel sits over the door and its neighbour
reasons.offset_mm: assumed: the west end of the north wall; which end the door is at is open

reasons.elevation_mm: Jim: the sleeping loft floor is 8 ft above the living floor
reasons.thickness_mm: the deck sheet gives it: deck_panel is the sold 23/32 in tongue-and-groove OSB, 4 by 8 ft (Jim, 2026-10-25: sold stock, nothing invented); a number here overrides it

reasons.member_width_mm: the joist stock gives it: joist_stock is the catalog's dressed 2x6 (wt.dressed_sizes); a number here overrides it
reasons.member_depth_mm: the joist stock gives it: joist_stock is the catalog's dressed 2x6 (wt.dressed_sizes); a number here overrides it
reasons.elevation_mm: the structural domain sets the joists' tops at the loft deck's elevation, so a null here takes it
reasons.bears_on: the south wall is glass from 4 ft up and the north wall's door rises to 8 ft, so the joists can only land on the solid west and east walls

reasons.member_width_mm: assumed: a ledger cut from the joist stock, fastened to the wall's inside face; the fastening is not checked
reasons.member_depth_mm: assumed: a ledger cut from the joist stock, as deep as the joists it carries

reasons.plies: assumed: two plies side by side, 3-1/2 in of LVL or 3 in of 2x lumber, fit inside the SIP's 3-5/8 in core (sip.prs610_core_thickness)

reasons.roof_dead_load_psf: assumed: 15 psf, the roof dead load Boise's roof-only header look-up assumes, research row gl.hdr.vl_lookup_roof_only; the roof build-up gives it
reasons.deflection_limit_ratio: assumed: span over 240, the live-load deflection limit of Boise's header tables, research row gl.hdr.vl_limits, applied to the whole load
reasons.roof_bears_on: assumed: the roof's 8 ft south hangover can only be carried by members running north-south across the south wall, so the roof bears on the south and north walls

reasons.exposure: assumed: the site's exposure category (B, C or D) is not in the sketch; no figure is chosen here

reasons.plies: assumed: a built-up beam of two 2x10 plies, 3 in wide, the stock every beam option is checked in

cost_usd.reason: Jim's soft target, 2026-10-20: soft idea limits
